title: Why You Should Allow Your Students To Socialize In Class
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin makes the case that brief, structured social breaks — around 60 to 90 seconds of permitted chatting — are a smart, deliberate management tool rather than a distraction to avoid. His central argument is that these short breaks clear students' minds of pent-up social thoughts so they can refocus more completely on the lesson, while also building the kind of likability that gives a teacher real leverage over behavior. He explicitly invokes the Law of Reciprocity: students who feel a teacher's kindness and understanding want to repay it through better behavior. The concrete technique is precise and bounded — the privilege must be explicitly taught and modeled, with clear rules about timing (once or twice daily for younger students, mid-period for older ones) and acceptable topics, never simply announced spontaneously. He warns that skipping the teaching step and just declaring "go ahead and talk" will backfire into more problems, not fewer. The overall claim is that occasional sanctioned socializing improves focus, reduces restlessness, and strengthens the relationship that makes consequences matter.
points: A permitted 60-90 second social break "clears the boards" so students can refocus fully on the lesson afterward.
Likability built through small social allowances gives a teacher real leverage over student behavior via reciprocity.
Short breaks are framed as a direct antidote to the restlessness and excitability that come from sitting too long.
The privilege must be explicitly taught and modeled with clear timing and topic boundaries — never opened up spontaneously.
quotes: However, when narrowly defined, giving your students the option to talk with their friends for a minute or two during the school day is a smart idea.
60-90 seconds or so is all it takes to “clear the boards.” It purges their thoughts from being dominated by what they desperately want to tell their friends.
Sitting too long causes excitability and restlessness. Short breaks throughout the day relax the body, clear the mind, and promote better listening and production.
It’s the Law of Reciprocity in action. Meaning, they’ll want to pay you back for your kindness and understanding.
You must teach and model exactly what one minute (or more) of socializing looks like.
